transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-11-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Rachel Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - HelixGuard), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Samir Kaur (InfoSec), Tom Becker (Devops), Maya (SRE intern)
Links referenced: Redwood SDK docs https://console.redwood.ai/sdk, SOC2 summary (sent on follow-up), demo notebook: /redwood/examples/onprem-proxy.ipynb

Auto-generated Summary (auto):
HelixGuard is evaluating options — likely to start with a Dedicated trial but must validate private on-prem deployment for regulated data. Key concerns: gateway/proxy pattern, SDK compatibility with LangChain and LlamaIndex, rate limiting/quotas on per-tenant basis, observability hooks (traces/metrics/alerts), KMS integration and audit logs. Next step is pricing docs + a short benchmark.

Topics:
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Edge/gateway proxy pattern and sidecar vs managed gateway
- SDK support and LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors
- Rate limits, quotas and token billing model
- Observability hooks and tracing / span correlation
- Security: SOC2, KMS, network topology (VPC / on-prem peering)

[00:00] Rachel Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Rachel, AE on the account, and Marco here is our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, Lena here, CTO at HelixGuard. We build anomaly detection for industrial control systems, lots of regulated customers, so data never leaves our private infra without controls.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Priya, platform. We own our ingress gateway and have a small edge fleet in two colo sites.
[00:28] Samir Kaur: Samir, InfoSec. I'm here for the security and compliance questions.
[00:33] Marco Diaz: Hi, Marco, Redwood SE, I work on private deployments and observability integrations.
[00:38] Rachel Chen: Great. Agenda — integration patterns, SDK/connector compatibility, rate limits, and next steps.

[01:05] Priya: Short context — we currently call OpenAI for some prototypes but want lower token cost and more control. We also ran into throughput spikes where our proxy chokes, so interested in batching and caching features.
[01:24] Rachel: Makes sense. Are you evaluating hosted first, or looking to jump straight to private on-prem?
[01:30] Lena: We need to pilot hosted to test functionality but primary goal is Private — air-gapped option or at least VPC peering. Legal requires we prove data residency.
[01:42] Tom Becker: We also want to validate a Dedicated path — reserved capacity with VPC peering might be quick.

[02:03] Marco: On the integration side, Redwood provides SDKs (python/js/go) and first-class connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Our SDK supports both direct REST and a lightweight proxy mode for sidecar deployments.
[02:20] Priya: Sidecar vs external gateway — what's the tradeoff?
[02:24] Marco: Sidecar keeps KV cache local to the app for lower latency, easier to implement prefix caching. Gateway gives centralized rate limiting, shared batching, and easier rollout across services. If you have an ingress gateway already, people often use a managed gateway in front of Redwood endpoints to control quotas. Both supported.
[02:42] Priya: When you say KV cache, is that the token cache? We do a lot of short-conversation use cases.
[02:48] Marco: K-V cache for key-value attention cache — keeps decoder state, reduces duplicated compute on repeated prefixes. In practise it's the KV cache; sorry sometimes my voice auto-corrects to K-V case.

[03:15] Samir: Security — how do you handle encryption in Private? KMS integrations? HSM?
[03:20] Marco: For Private on-prem, you bring your KMS; we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-hosted vaults via KMS adapters. There's an HSM option for Dedicated/Private for pay-by-SLA customers. We also provide audit logs with token-level redaction options.
[03:38] Samir: And SOC2 / ISO?
[03:40] Rachel: We have SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane; private deployments inherit customer controls. We'll send over the SOC2 summary and our security integration guide.

[04:10] Lena: Observability — we need span correlation back to our traces (jaeger/otel) and per-request token cost reporting.
[04:18] Marco: We export traces in OpenTelemetry. You can correlate request_id from your gateway with Redwood traces. We also provide per-token cost headers and a cost API that reports token breakdown by model and prompt.
[04:33] Maya: Is there a webhook or streaming telemetry?
[04:36] Marco: Streaming metrics via Prometheus remote write in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted you get metrics and a webhook for alerts.

[05:05] Priya: Rate limits — we need per-tenant quotas, burst control, and graceful degradation. Can Redwood enforce that?
[05:11] Marco: Yes, you can set multi-level policies: global, customer-tenant, and route-level. We support token-based quotas and RPS quotas. Also automatic fallback to smaller model variants if Dedicated pool is overloaded — and you can configure fallback policy.
[05:26] Priya: Fallbacks are good, but we need deterministic SLOs — if you route to a lower-quality model, how do you signal that to the app?
[05:34] Marco: The SDK returns metadata headers: model_used, fallbacks_applied, and estimated_quality_score — app can decide to fail-open or fail-closed.

[06:00] Tom: Architecture — we currently run an envoy-based gateway. Can we route traffic to Redwood via a proxy? Any sample configs?
[06:08] Marco: Yes, we have sample envoy + kong configs. The typical pattern is envoy -> internal gateway -> Redwood sidecar or public endpoint with VPC peering. We'll share the repo link.
[06:20] Rachel: (link note) repo: github.com/redwood/integration-samples/envoy-proxy-example

[06:40] Lena: LangChain/LlamaIndex — does your SDK play nicely with chains and indexes? Any custom tokenizers or embedding formats?
[06:47] Marco: We support the embeddings API compatible with common tooling. For LlamaIndex we provide an adapter that handles text chunking and embedding batching. For LangChain we have an LLM wrapper so you can plug Redwood like any other provider. There are a couple of minor name swaps in older SDK versions but the latest release fixed them.
[07:04] Priya: Do you support streaming responses for chains?
[07:07] Marco: Yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and via SSE/HTTP. Chains that do stepwise decoding will see tokens as they arrive.

[07:30] Samir: On telemetry, we need PII scrubbing from logs. How are logs emitted in Private?
[07:36] Marco: In Private you control logs; we provide structured logs with PII scrubbing options on the ingestion pipeline. By default we mask emails and credit-card-like strings. You can also provide a custom redaction regex.

[08:02] Lena: Latency targets — we need p50 < 80ms for small prompts and p95 < 250ms for the primary flow. Is that realistic?
[08:10] Marco: For hosted short prompts on large models p50 under 80ms is tight; usually p50 for small models/short sequences is closer to 30-60ms with our optimized runtime, p95 depends heavily on batching and KV utilization. For Dedicated with reserved GPU and smart routing we can tune for those SLOs. We'll need the prompt set and RPS to give an accurate projection.
[08:28] Tom: Any built-in quantization support? We use mixed precision on prem.
[08:33] Marco: The runtime supports INT8/FP16 quantization paths and custom kernel selection. For on-prem you can select quantized model builds — we advise testing quality regression.

[09:01] Priya: About token billing — we bill by tokens in Hosted, but for Dedicated/Private is it flat capacity vs per-token mix?
[09:09] Rachel: Hosted is per-token. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity (monthly) plus a small per-token overage. Private licensing is an enterprise fee plus optional usage-based components depending on deployment. We'll include sample SKUs in the pricing doc.

[09:36] Maya: Can we use our own models behind Redwood or does it only host Redwoods verified models?
[09:41] Marco: In Private you can bring-your-own model (BYOM) — we support custom model artifacts and model registry. In Hosted we offer curated models; Dedicated can run customer models under a guarded surface.

[10:05] Priya: Dev experience — how fast are SDKs to get started? Any quickstart or notebook?
[10:10] Marco: The python SDK has a 5-line quickstart; we have a demo notebook for sidecar proxy and a LangChain example that we can share. For connector maturity: LangChain adapter is GA, LlamaIndex adapter is beta.

[10:40] Samir: Legal/procurement — we need contracts for on-prem and details about data processing addendum. Who handles that?
[10:47] Rachel: Our legal ops handles DPAs and enterprise contracts. For Private on-prem customers we have a standard enterprise agreement and we'll work with you on any custom clauses. I'll loop in legal after the pricing step.

[11:10] Priya: Are there any rate limiting pitfalls we've hit before with proxy setups?
[11:15] Marco: Common mistakes: putting coarse-grained batching on gateway that creates head-of-line latency, or using single shared KV caches across multitenant workloads causing cache thrash. We recommend per-tenant caches or namespace isolation. Also watch sequence length distribution — it can blow up token costs.

[11:45] Lena: For the benchmark, can you simulate our RPS profile? We have a spikey pattern: baseline 20 RPS, bursts to 400 RPS for 20s every 5 minutes.
[11:58] Marco: Yes, we'll run a replay using your histogram. If you send prompt samples we can mirror sequence length distribution and simulate bursts with our load harness.

[12:18] Tom: Networking — VPC peering vs private interconnect? Latency difference?
[12:23] Marco: VPC peering is simplest and usually good for many customers. Private interconnect or direct connect gives lower and more consistent latency — preferred for strict SLOs. For on-prem air-gapped installs there is no peering — it's all internal.

[12:50] Priya: Observability hooks — which headers should we propagate to correlate?
[12:55] Marco: Propagate x-request-id, x-customer-id, x-route, and x-prefix-key if you're using caching. Then map that to the Redwood span id in traces.

[13:12] Maya: Any gotchas with LangChain memory + Redwood caching?
[13:17] Marco: If you rely on LangChain's in-memory buffer and also enable prefix caching at runtime you might double-store state; it's fine but monitor memory. We usually defer caching to runtime for better hit rates.

[13:42] Samir: Compliance — can we run an audit test? We need to see audit logs for 90 days.
[13:47] Marco: For Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies; audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via syslog or cloud forwarders. We'll provide an example retention policy.

[14:10] Rachel: Quick recap — we will: send pricing and SKUs, security docs, sample envoy configs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter examples, and spin up a benchmark after we receive prompts and RPS histogram.
[14:24] Lena: Sounds good. Also can you include a sample VPC peering network diagram?
[14:28] Rachel: Yes, will attach.

[14:40] Priya: One last thing — support model pinning across rollouts, we need immutable versions for traceability.
[14:47] Marco: You can pin model versions per route and we keep model version metadata in the audit logs. Rollouts are canary/A-B with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

[15:05] Tom: Who's the day-to-day contact if we hit issues during a pilot?
[15:09] Rachel: I'll be your AE for procurement/contracting, Marco will be SE contact for technical onboarding. We'll also assign an onboarding CSM if you sign a Dedicated pilot.

[15:30] Lena: OK let's pause there and we'll send the prompt set and RPS. Appreciate this — it's the clearest integration map we've seen.
[15:37] Rachel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and pricing.

[15:50] (meeting ends)
